sources.title: EV Database - Tesla Model Y Long Range AWD (2022-2025, UK/EU listing)
sources.notes: European (LG 5L cells, NMC) listing: nominal 78.1 / useable 75 kWh (estimated by the site), 400 V, 250 kW DC, 11 kW AC, preconditioning automatic when navigating to a charger. Site says Tesla does not publish official figures.

sources.title: EV Database - Tesla Model Y Performance (2022-2025)
sources.notes: Nominal 78.1 / useable 75 kWh, NMC (LG 5L), 400 V, 250 kW DC, 11 kW AC, preconditioning possible and automatic with navigation. European listing.

sources.title: EV Database - Tesla Model Y RWD (CATL 6L, 2022-2024)
sources.notes: CATL LFP: nominal 60 / useable 57 kWh (estimated), 340 V nominal (400 V architecture), 170 kW DC, 11 kW AC, preconditioning automatic with navigation. InsideEVs/Electrek say the Canadian 2023 RWD is this Shanghai-built LFP car.

sources.title: EV Database - Tesla Model Y RWD (Juniper, CATL 6M, 2025)
sources.notes: Standard (LFP) Juniper RWD, European listing: nominal 64 / useable 60 kWh, 175 kW DC, 11 kW AC, 400 V class.

sources.title: EV Database - Tesla Model Y Premium RWD (Juniper, LG 5L, 2025-2026)
sources.notes: Successor of the Long Range RWD: nominal 78.1 / useable 75 kWh (estimated), NMC, 250 kW DC, 11 kW AC, 400 V. European listing.

sources.title: EV Database - Tesla Model Y Premium RWD (Juniper, Tesla 4680, 2026)
sources.notes: Nominal 79 / useable 74 kWh, NMC, 4680 cells (828 cells, 92s9p), 250 kW DC, 11 kW AC, 400 V, preconditioning automatic with navigation. European listing, available since April 2026.

sources.title: ArenaEV - Tesla Model Y LR AWD 82 kWh (2021-2025)
sources.notes: 82 kWh total / 75 kWh usable, 250 kW DC (Supercharger V3), 11 kW AC. Regional prices include USD.

sources.title: ArenaEV - Tesla Model Y AWD (2026 onward)
sources.notes: Standard AWD: 69 kWh total, liquid-cooled LFP (400 V type), Supercharger 225 kW max, 11 kW AC. Page carries US weight/trunk figures.

sources.title: ArenaEV - Tesla Model Y Standard (2025 onward)
sources.notes: Standard (RWD): 69 kWh total, LFP (400 V type), Supercharger 225 kW max, 11 kW AC. Released October 2025; US weight/trunk figures.

sources.title: InsideEVs - What Batteries Are Tesla Using In Its Electric Cars?
sources.notes: Panasonic 2170 NCA cells for Model 3/Y from California; LGES 2170 NCM for Shanghai- and Berlin-built Model Y; CATL LFP for entry-level cars; Texas 4680 chemistry undisclosed.

sources.title: Teslabs - Tesla manual preconditioning: how does it work (2025-01-24)
sources.notes: Says Tesla has no feature to manually precondition the battery (menu or app); only navigating to a Supercharger starts it. One June 2025 comment (Model 3) disagrees. No model years given.

sources.title: Wikipedia - Tesla Model Y
sources.notes: All versions up to 11.5 kW AC and up to 250 kW DC (225 kW on Standard); standard-range cars LFP, Long Range/Performance nickel-based; Performance Juniper LG 5M pack ~82-84 kWh usable; Model Y L AU/NZ 88.2 kWh gross / ~84 usable.

sources.title: Wikipedia - North American Charging Standard
sources.notes: Tesla used its proprietary connector (now NACS) on all vehicles since the 2012 Model S, listing the Model Y.

sources.title: EVSpecifications - 2021 Tesla Model Y Standard Range RWD
sources.notes: 52.4 kWh (gross/net not stated), NCA, Panasonic 21700, 360 V, 170 kW DC, 11.5 kW AC, NACS. The page also says "not released to the market", so reliability is low.

sources.title: Not a Tesla App - Tesla launches 6-seat Model Y L in the US
sources.notes: US Model Y L (Premium AWD Launch Series): 83 kWh pack (gross/usable not stated), 250 kW peak Supercharging, EPA 325 mi (19 in).

battery.capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists nominal 78.1 kWh for the 2022-2025 Long Range AWD (European, LG-cell). Tesla publishes no pack size; the North American Fremont (Panasonic) pack is assumed the same 75 kWh-class pack (ArenaEV 82/75 for the LR AWD 2021-2025 too).

battery.capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database useable 75 kWh (itself an estimate); not Fremont-specific, assumed the same for 2020-2023 NA cars.
Estimated: ArenaEV 82 kWh total / 75 kWh usable for the Model Y LR AWD 2021-2025.

battery.chemistry.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs: Panasonic 2170 NCA cells go into Model 3/Y built in California (Fremont). Applied to the 2020-2023 Fremont Long Range / Performance.

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists a 400 V architecture (357 V nominal) for the same-generation Long Range AWD.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: ArenaEV lists 250 kW Supercharger V3 for the Model Y LR AWD 2021-2025; EV Database lists 250 kW for LR AWD and Performance.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia: all Model Y versions charge on AC up to 11.5 kW (North American 48 A single-phase); European listings say 11 kW.

battery.preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Teslabs (2025-01) says no manual battery-preconditioning control exists, only navigating to a charger; EV Database listings say the battery is warmed automatically when navigating to a charger. Tesla manuals were not fetchable (403). Navigation preconditioning is an over-the-air software feature across Tesla models; Teslabs gives no model years.
Estimated: Listing for the same model family says preconditioning is possible and starts automatically when navigating to a charger. Combined with the Teslabs no-manual-control statement.

charge_port.notes: Estimated: Tesla has used its own connector (now NACS) on all its North American cars since 2012, including the Model Y (2020 on). Not read on a Tesla page for this model year.

supercharger_access.notes: Estimated: Tesla-built cars with the Tesla/NACS inlet can use the Supercharger network; page says every Model Y uses native NACS. Applied to this model year as a lineup-wide fact.
